_meta.indication: ERLEADA is indicated for the treatment of patients with non-metastatic, castration-resistant prostate cancer (NM-CRPC).

pivotal_trials.design: Multinational, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 study of apalutamide 240 mg daily vs placebo, both with concurrent GnRH analog or bilateral orchiectomy.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with high-risk non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (NM-CRPC), defined by PSA doubling time ≤ 10 months.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Metastasis-free survival (MFS) per Blinded Independent Central Review was the primary endpoint.
pivotal_trials.n: 1207 patients randomized 2:1 to apalutamide (N=806) or placebo (N=401).
pivotal_trials.result: Median MFS 40.5 months with apalutamide vs 16.2 months with placebo; HR 0.28 (95% CI 0.23, 0.35), p<0.0001.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥10%) were fatigue, hypertension, rash, diarrhea, nausea, weight decreased, arthralgia, fall, hot flush, decreased appetite, fracture, and peripheral edema. Fatigue occurred in 39% (vs 28% placebo) and rash in 24% (vs 6% placebo). ERLEADA was discontinued for adverse reactions in 11% of patients, most commonly rash (3%).
target_moa: Apalutamide is an androgen receptor (AR) inhibitor that binds directly to the ligand-binding domain of the AR, inhibiting AR nuclear translocation, DNA binding, and AR-mediated transcription.
modality: Small molecule (orally bioavailable New Molecular Entity).

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee Meeting was held for this application.

summary.text: ERLEADA (apalutamide) received Priority review and Fast Track designation (granted to IND 104676 on August 11, 2017). It was approved via the traditional pathway based on the SPARTAN phase 3 trial, with no advisory committee meeting held for this application.
